headline: Medium-risk shared-workspace and output-trust pathways exist; no critical compliance or irreversible default harm is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so malicious content in files or MCP outputs could influence its prompts. pdf.js processes PDF files and can surface attacker-controlled document text. The pair has a plausible file-based bridge, but no direct shared channel is documented, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Continue ingests PDF-derived text from shared workspace files or MCP output without sanitization
IF pdf.js renders attacker-controlled PDF content that is then copied into Continue prompts
mitigations: Restrict shared folders to trusted documents only
Disable MCP servers that emit untrusted text
Use a manual review step before pasting PDF text into Continue
Open PDFs in a separate workspace from coding tasks
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between pdf.js output and Continue input

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write/read workspace files, while pdf.js reads PDF files. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive code or document contents can flow between them through files. No evidence shows uncontrolled third-party upload by pdf.js, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF PDF contents or source code are stored in files accessible to both agents
mitigations: Separate code and PDF workspaces
Limit Continue to a narrow project folder
Store sensitive PDFs outside the shared workspace
Review file permissions before running both agents
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write and broad network egress, while pdf.js has browser execution but no network egress and no write capability is listed. The profiles do not show overlapping unrestricted writes to the same mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually points both agents at the same writable directory
IF browser-based pdf.js tests are configured to modify shared files
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories
Run pdf.js tests in a separate temp folder
Keep Continue on read-only access where possible
Check for accidental concurrent edits before saving
requires-engineering: add file locking for shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or instructions from workspace context, and pdf.js can present document content in a browser-based worker. If pdf.js output is treated as authoritative input to Continue, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. No explicit verification boundary is documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into Continue as trusted facts
IF Continue is allowed to act on document-derived claims without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on PDF-derived claims
Mark pdf.js output as untrusted in the workflow
Use citations or source links when transferring facts
Disable auto-apply actions from Continue
requires-engineering: add verification gates between document parsing and agent actions

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles show no PHI, residency, or certification mismatch. Continue handles model provider API keys and workspace files, while pdf.js only touches PDF files. With no documented compliance conflict, residual risk is low and limited to policy alignment checks.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the shared workspace
IF the chosen model provider for Continue has stricter residency or retention rules than the PDF workflow
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Confirm provider retention settings for Continue
Use local inference for sensitive documents
Document a data-handling policy for PDFs and code
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
